symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of units in the fixed finite population.

symbols.name: V_n
symbols.def: Finite population \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Generic outcome-unit index.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Generic assignment-coordinate index.

symbols.name: \Omega_n
symbols.def: Binary assignment space \(\Omega_n=\{0,1\}^{V_n}\).

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: Generic global assignment.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Fixed interior-overlap constant.

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Source probability used in the separating hub family.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Target probability used in the separating hub family.

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.def: Known vector of source Bernoulli probabilities.

symbols.name: \pi'
symbols.def: Known vector of target Bernoulli probabilities.

symbols.name: p_{\pi}(z)
symbols.def: Source probability mass at assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: p_{\pi'}(z)
symbols.def: Target probability mass at assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_i
symbols.def: Known assignment coordinates on which unit \(i\)'s schedule may depend.

symbols.name: X_i
symbols.def: Local assignment cells \(X_i=\{0,1\}^{\Gamma_i}\).

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: Generic local assignment cell.

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: Generic local Fourier subset.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: Generic subset of a retained Fourier index.

symbols.name: \mathcal S_i
symbols.def: Known finite family of retained local Fourier subsets.

symbols.name: \chi_{i,U}^{\pi}
symbols.def: Source-policy biased Fourier character constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local-fourier-character}\).

symbols.name: H_i
symbols.def: Span of the retained characters, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local-fourier-space}\).

symbols.name: v_i
symbols.def: Fixed local potential-outcome schedule for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: For the fixed \(n\)-unit instance, \(E=\bigoplus_{i\in V_n}H_i\) is equipped with the product-\(L^2\) inner product \(\langle f,g\rangle_E=\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)f_i(z_{\Gamma_i})g_i(z_{\Gamma_i})\). Source positivity makes this an inner product, so \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: Schedule vector \(v=(v_i)_{i\in V_n}\).

symbols.name: K_i
symbols.def: Bounded local Fourier evaluation polytope constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local-evaluation-polytope}\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Product schedule class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bounded-fourier-class}\).

symbols.name: Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: Observed outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})\) at the realized source assignment.

symbols.name: p_{\pi',i}(x)
symbols.def: Target-policy probability of local cell \(x\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local-target-mass}\).

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: Target-policy expected average outcome constructed in \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\).

symbols.name: o_z(v)
symbols.def: Vector of all unit outcomes revealed at assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: N_z
symbols.def: Linear selector satisfying \(N_zv=o_z(v)\).

symbols.name: \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V_n}
symbols.def: The Euclidean inner product \(\langle r,s\rangle_{V_n}=\sum_{i\in V_n}r_is_i\) on \(\mathbb R^{V_n}\).

symbols.name: N_z^{\ast}
symbols.def: The unique adjoint of \(N_z\) relative to \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_E\) and \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V_n}\), characterized by \(\langle N_zf,r\rangle_{V_n}=\langle f,N_z^{\ast}r\rangle_E\) for every \(f\in E\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb S_+^E
symbols.def: The cone \(\mathbb S_+^E=\{M\in\mathcal L(E):M=M^{\ast},\ \langle f,Mf\rangle_E\ge0\text{ for every }f\in E\}\), where the operator adjoint is taken in the Hilbert geometry of \(E\).

symbols.name: a_z
symbols.def: Linear weights used after assignment \(z\) is observed.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Collection \(a=(a_z)_{z\in\Omega_n}\).

symbols.name: \delta_a
symbols.def: Assignment-indexed linear estimator constructed in \(\mathrm{def:semilinear-rule}\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: Finite linear-minimax frontier constructed in \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: Generic Borel measurable estimator based on the assignment and observed outcomes.

symbols.name: R^{\star}
symbols.def: All-measurable-estimator minimax frontier constructed in \(\mathrm{def:unrestricted-frontier}\).

symbols.name: \ell
symbols.def: The unique Riesz vector in the specified Hilbert geometry satisfying \(\theta(v)=\langle\ell,v\rangle_E\) for every \(v\in E\).

symbols.name: a^{\star}
symbols.def: A minimizer of the finite program defining \(F\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{clip}
symbols.def: Projection \(\operatorname{clip}(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{inc}}
symbols.def: Clipped estimator constructed in \(\mathrm{def:clipped-incidence-estimator}\).

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: Countably additive probability law supported on genuine bounded schedules.

symbols.name: \mathbf V
symbols.def: Random bounded schedule with law \(\nu\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B(\nu)
symbols.def: Average posterior-variance certificate constructed in \(\mathrm{def:prior-certificate}\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{UB}(a)
symbols.def: Worst-case risk of a feasible assignment-indexed linear rule.

symbols.name: \operatorname{LB}(\nu)
symbols.def: Lower certificate \(\operatorname{LB}(\nu)=\mathcal B(\nu)\).

symbols.name: c_0
symbols.def: Numerical constant independent of the population, graph, policies, and supports.

symbols.name: \mathcal I
symbols.def: Bipartite assignment-to-outcome incidence graph constructed in \(\mathrm{def:incidence-graph}\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{tw}(\mathcal I)
symbols.def: Treewidth of the bipartite exposure-incidence graph.

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound on incidence treewidth.

symbols.name: L_{\mathrm{in}}
symbols.def: Bit length of rational policies and explicitly listed local support and vertex tables.

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: Known graph on vertex set \(V_n\) in the \(n\)-th experiment.

symbols.name: \pi_n
symbols.def: Known source product-Bernoulli probability vector in the \(n\)-th experiment.

symbols.name: \pi'_n
symbols.def: Known target product-Bernoulli probability vector in the \(n\)-th experiment.

symbols.name: p_{\pi_n}(z)
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) source mass \(p_{\pi_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\).

symbols.name: p_{\pi'_n}(z)
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) target mass \(p_{\pi'_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi'_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi'_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{n,i}
symbols.def: Known local assignment neighborhood of outcome unit \(i\) in graph \(G_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal S_{n,i}
symbols.def: Known finite downward-closed local Fourier support of unit \(i\) in the \(n\)-th experiment.

symbols.name: X_{n,i}
symbols.def: Local assignment cells \(X_{n,i}=\{0,1\}^{\Gamma_{n,i}}\) in row \(n\).

symbols.name: H_{n,i}
symbols.def: The space \(H_{n,i}=\operatorname{span}\{x\mapsto\prod_{j\in U}(x_j-(\pi_n)_j)/\sqrt{(\pi_n)_j(1-(\pi_n)_j)}:U\in\mathcal S_{n,i}\}\).

symbols.name: E_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) direct-sum schedule space equipped with the product-\(L^2\) inner product constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-hilbert-geometry}\).

symbols.name: \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{E_n}
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) product-\(L^2\) inner product under the source law, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-hilbert-geometry}\).

symbols.name: v_n
symbols.def: A fixed row-\(n\) schedule vector \(v_n=(v_{n,i})_{i\in V_n}\).

symbols.name: \theta_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) target-policy functional constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-target-selector-geometry}\).

symbols.name: N_{n,z}
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) evaluation selector constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-target-selector-geometry}\).

symbols.name: N_{n,z}^{\ast}
symbols.def: The adjoint of \(N_{n,z}\) relative to \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{E_n}\) and the Euclidean inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V_n}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb S_+^{E_n}
symbols.def: The cone of self-adjoint positive semidefinite operators on the row-\(n\) Hilbert space, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-psd-riesz-geometry}\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: For a fixed row \(n\), a generic positive semidefinite self-adjoint operator \(M\) on the Hilbert space \(E_n\).

symbols.name: \ell_n
symbols.def: The unique Riesz vector for \(\theta_n\) in the row-\(n\) product-\(L^2\) geometry, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-psd-riesz-geometry}\).

symbols.name: K_{n,i}
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) local evaluation polytope constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-bounded-fourier-class}\).

symbols.name: K_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) bounded schedule class \(K_n=\prod_{i\in V_n}K_{n,i}\subset E_n\), constructed from \(\pi_n\), \(\Gamma_{n,i}\), and \(\mathcal S_{n,i}\).

symbols.name: a_{n,z}
symbols.def: Linear weight vector used after assignment \(z\) in row \(n\).

symbols.name: a_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) collection \(a_n=(a_{n,z})_{z\in\Omega_n}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak M_n(K_n)
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) convex moment body constructed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-body}\).

symbols.name: \psi_{n,z}(M)
symbols.def: The row-\(n\), assignment-specific generalized least-squares residual, with domain and pseudoinverse convention fixed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) moment-body dual value constructed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak M(K)
symbols.def: Convex hull of rank-one schedule moments constructed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-body}\).

symbols.name: \psi_z(M)
symbols.def: Assignment-specific generalized least-squares residual constructed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: Moment-body dual value constructed in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{prior}}
symbols.def: Structure-preserving prior-rounding handle constructed in \(\mathrm{def:prior-rounding-handle}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{tw}}
symbols.def: Bag-local moment and epigraph elimination handle constructed in \(\mathrm{def:treewidth-handle}\).

symbols.name: F_n
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) linear frontier defined directly from \(E_n\), \(K_n\), \(N_{n,z}\), \(\theta_n\), and source policy \(\pi_n\) in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-frontiers}\).

symbols.name: R_n^{\star}
symbols.def: The row-\(n\) unrestricted minimax risk defined directly from \(E_n\), \(K_n\), \(N_{n,z}\), \(\theta_n\), and source policy \(\pi_n\) in \(\mathrm{def:indexed-frontiers}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak A
symbols.def: The sequence \(\mathfrak A=((G_n,\pi_n,\pi'_n,(\Gamma_{n,i},\mathcal S_{n,i},X_{n,i},H_{n,i},K_{n,i})_{i\in V_n},E_n,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{E_n},\theta_n,(N_{n,z},N_{n,z}^{\ast})_{z\in\Omega_n},K_n,F_n,R_n^{\star}))_{n\ge1}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf{Adm}
symbols.def: Class of admissible triangular arrays constructed in \(\mathrm{def:admissible-triangular-array}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf C(c_0,\mathfrak A)
symbols.def: Uniform comparison predicate constructed in \(\mathrm{def:common-comparison}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{hub}}
symbols.def: Overlapping additive-hub family constructed in \(\mathrm{def:hub-family}\).

symbols.name: D_n^{\mathrm{LE}}
symbols.def: The exact spectral-overlap degree \(D_n^{\mathrm{LE}}=\max_{i\in V_n}|\{j\in V_n\setminus\{i\}:\Gamma_i\cap\Gamma_j\ne\varnothing\}|\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def:loomba-eckles-spectral-envelope}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of assignment-independent copies of a fixed local motif.

symbols.name: \mathfrak m
symbols.def: A fixed finite source-target Fourier observation motif.

symbols.name: u_{\mathfrak m}
symbols.def: A bounded unbiased local rule for the motif target.

symbols.name: \nu_{\mathfrak m}
symbols.def: A symmetric genuine prior supported on the motif schedule class.

symbols.name: \sigma_{\mathfrak m}^2
symbols.def: Worst-case risk of \(u_{\mathfrak m}\) on one motif.

symbols.name: b_{\mathfrak m}
symbols.def: Positive one-motif posterior ambiguity under \(\nu_{\mathfrak m}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak m^{\sqcup m}
symbols.def: Disjoint union of \(m\) assignment-independent copies of \(\mathfrak m\), with the target averaged across copies.

symbols.name: F_m^{\sqcup}
symbols.def: Linear frontier for \(\mathfrak m^{\sqcup m}\).

symbols.name: R_m^{\star,\sqcup}
symbols.def: Unrestricted minimax risk for \(\mathfrak m^{\sqcup m}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_U^{\pi,\pi'}
symbols.def: The coefficient \(\Delta_U^{\pi,\pi'}=\prod_{j\in U}(\pi'_j-\pi_j)/\sqrt{\pi_j(1-\pi_j)}\), with empty product one, loading the source-policy Fourier character indexed by \(U\) under the target policy.

symbols.name: W_i^{\mathrm{LE}}
symbols.def: The Loomba--Eckles retained-support spectral transport weight constructed in \(\mathrm{def:loomba-eckles-spectral-envelope}\).

symbols.name: B_n^{\mathrm{LE}}
symbols.def: The smallest uniform bounded-class second-moment envelope for the Loomba--Eckles unit EAO summands, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:loomba-eckles-spectral-envelope}\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Generic bounded-schedule direction used in a selector fiber.

symbols.name: M^{\star}
symbols.def: When \(F>0\), a maximizer of \(\mathcal D\) having minimum rank among all maximizers.

symbols.name: r_{\star}
symbols.def: For \(F>0\), \(r_{\star}=\operatorname{rank}(M^{\star})\); for \(F=0\), \(r_{\star}=1\).

symbols.name: \rho_z
symbols.def: Maximum absolute target contrast among bounded schedules invisible under selector \(N_z\).

symbols.name: S_{\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Source-probability-weighted sum of squared selector-fiber radii.

symbols.name: m_{\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Largest source-probability-weighted squared selector-fiber radius.

symbols.name: \kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Ratio \(S_{\mathrm{fib}}/m_{\mathrm{fib}}\) when \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), and one otherwise.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Minimum of the dual-rank and effective-fiber complexities, with value one in the zero-fiber case.

symbols.name: \nu_z
symbols.def: A symmetric genuine prior supported on a pair of opposite schedules in \(K\cap\ker N_z\) attaining \(\rho_z\).

symbols.name: M_n^{\star}
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) minimum-rank maximizer of \(\mathcal D_n\) when \(F_n>0\).

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) version of \(r_{\star}\).

symbols.name: \rho_{n,z}
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) selector-fiber radius for assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: S_{n,\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) source-weighted sum of squared fiber radii.

symbols.name: m_{n,\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) largest source-weighted squared fiber radius.

symbols.name: \kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) effective selector-fiber count.

symbols.name: \kappa_n
symbols.def: Row-\(n\) minimum of the rank and effective-fiber complexities, with the zero-case convention.

symbols.name: p_n
symbols.def: Homogeneous source probability used in the row-\(n\) member of the local-policy hub sequence.

symbols.name: q_n
symbols.def: Homogeneous target probability used in the row-\(n\) member of the local-policy hub sequence.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Scalar epigraph variable in the fully expanded frontier program.

assumptions.condition: The source assignment mass satisfies \(p_{\pi}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}\pi_j^{z_j}(1-\pi_j)^{1-z_j}\) for every \(z\in\Omega_n\).
The source probabilities satisfy \(\varepsilon\le\pi_j\le1-\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in V_n\).
The target assignment mass satisfies \(p_{\pi'}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi'_j)^{z_j}(1-\pi'_j)^{1-z_j}\) for every \(z\in\Omega_n\).
The target probabilities satisfy \(\varepsilon\le\pi'_j\le1-\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in V_n\).
Each retained support is downward closed: if \(U\in\mathcal S_i\) and \(W\subseteq U\), then \(W\in\mathcal S_i\).
For every \(i\in V_n\), the local schedule satisfies \(v_i\in H_i\).
The schedule vector \(v\) is fixed before the source assignment \(z\) is drawn.

definitions.name: Source-policy local Fourier character
definitions.construction: For \(x\in X_i\) and \(U\subseteq\Gamma_i\), set \(\chi_{i,U}^{\pi}(x)=\prod_{j\in U}(x_j-\pi_j)/\sqrt{\pi_j(1-\pi_j)}\), with \(\chi_{i,\varnothing}^{\pi}=1\).

definitions.name: Retained local Fourier space
definitions.construction: \(H_i=\operatorname{span}\{\chi_{i,U}^{\pi}:U\in\mathcal S_i\}\subseteq\mathbb R^{X_i}\).

definitions.name: Bounded local Fourier evaluation polytope
definitions.construction: \(K_i=\{v_i\in H_i: |v_i(x)|\le1\text{ for every }x\in X_i\}\).

definitions.name: Bounded local-Fourier schedule class
definitions.construction: \(K=\{v=(v_i)_{i\in V_n}\in E: v_i\in H_i\text{ and }|v_i(x)|\le1\text{ for every }i\in V_n,\ x\in X_i\}=\prod_{i\in V_n}K_i\).

definitions.name: Target local-cell probability
definitions.construction: \(p_{\pi',i}(x)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n:z_{\Gamma_i}=x}p_{\pi'}(z)\).

definitions.name: Target-policy expected average outcome
definitions.construction: \(\theta(v)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x)\).

definitions.name: Selector observation operator
definitions.construction: For each \(z\in\Omega_n\), \(N_z:E\to\mathbb R^{V_n}\) is defined by \((N_zv)_i=v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})\), so \(o_z(v)=N_zv\).

definitions.name: Assignment-indexed linear rule
definitions.construction: For \(a=(a_z)_{z\in\Omega_n}\), define \(\delta_a(z,N_zv)=a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv\).

definitions.name: Probability-weighted Fourier exposure-incidence frontier
definitions.construction: \(F=\inf_{a\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}\sup_{v\in K}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2\).

definitions.name: Unrestricted design-based minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R^{\star}=\inf_{\delta\ \mathrm{Borel}}\sup_{v\in K}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\bigl(\delta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2\).

definitions.name: Indexed product-\(L^2\) schedule Hilbert space
definitions.construction: For every \(n\ge1\) and \(i\in V_n\), let \(X_{n,i}=\{0,1\}^{\Gamma_{n,i}}\) and \(H_{n,i}=\operatorname{span}\{x\mapsto\prod_{j\in U}(x_j-(\pi_n)_j)/\sqrt{(\pi_n)_j(1-(\pi_n)_j)}:U\in\mathcal S_{n,i}\}\). Define \(E_n=\bigoplus_{i\in V_n}H_{n,i}\) and, for \(f,g\in E_n\), \(\langle f,g\rangle_{E_n}=\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi_n}(z)f_i(z_{\Gamma_{n,i}})g_i(z_{\Gamma_{n,i}})\), where \(p_{\pi_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\). Also fix \(\langle r,s\rangle_{V_n}=\sum_{i\in V_n}r_is_i\) on \(\mathbb R^{V_n}\). Positivity of \(\pi_n\) makes \(E_n\) a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.

definitions.name: Indexed target functional, selector, and adjoint
definitions.construction: For every \(n\ge1\), define \(\theta_n(v_n)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi'_n}(z)v_{n,i}(z_{\Gamma_{n,i}})\), where \(p_{\pi'_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi'_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi'_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\). For each \(z\in\Omega_n\), define \(N_{n,z}:E_n\to\mathbb R^{V_n}\) by \((N_{n,z}v_n)_i=v_{n,i}(z_{\Gamma_{n,i}})\). Its adjoint \(N_{n,z}^{\ast}:\mathbb R^{V_n}\to E_n\) is the unique linear map satisfying \(\langle N_{n,z}f,r\rangle_{V_n}=\langle f,N_{n,z}^{\ast}r\rangle_{E_n}\) for every \(f\in E_n\) and \(r\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\).

definitions.name: Indexed positive cone and target Riesz vector
definitions.construction: For each \(n\), define \(\mathbb S_+^{E_n}=\{M\in\mathcal L(E_n):M=M^{\ast},\ \langle f,Mf\rangle_{E_n}\ge0\text{ for every }f\in E_n\}\). Define \(\ell_n\in E_n\) as the unique vector satisfying \(\theta_n(v_n)=\langle\ell_n,v_n\rangle_{E_n}\) for every \(v_n\in E_n\).

definitions.name: Indexed bounded local-Fourier schedule class
definitions.construction: For every \(n\ge1\), \(K_{n,i}=\{h\in H_{n,i}:|h(x)|\le1\text{ for every }x\in X_{n,i}\}\) and \(K_n=\{v_n=(v_{n,i})_{i\in V_n}\in E_n:v_{n,i}\in K_{n,i}\text{ for every }i\in V_n\}=\prod_{i\in V_n}K_{n,i}\subset E_n\).

definitions.name: Indexed linear and unrestricted minimax frontiers
definitions.construction: For every \(n\ge1\), define \(F_n=\inf_{a_n\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}\sup_{v_n\in K_n}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi_n}(z)\bigl(a_{n,z}^{\mathsf T}N_{n,z}v_n-\theta_n(v_n)\bigr)^2\) and \(R_n^{\star}=\inf_{\delta\ \mathrm{Borel}}\sup_{v_n\in K_n}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi_n}(z)\bigl(\delta(z,N_{n,z}v_n)-\theta_n(v_n)\bigr)^2\).

definitions.name: Admissible triangular array
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Adm}=\{\mathfrak A=((G_n,\pi_n,\pi'_n,(\Gamma_{n,i},\mathcal S_{n,i},X_{n,i},H_{n,i},K_{n,i})_{i\in V_n},E_n,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{E_n},\theta_n,(N_{n,z},N_{n,z}^{\ast})_{z\in\Omega_n},K_n,F_n,R_n^{\star}))_{n\ge1}:\text{ for every }n,\ G_n\text{ is a known graph on }V_n,\ \Gamma_{n,i}\subseteq V_n\text{ is known for every }i,\ p_{\pi_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\text{ and }p_{\pi'_n}(z)=\prod_{j\in V_n}(\pi'_n)_j^{z_j}(1-(\pi'_n)_j)^{1-z_j}\text{ with one common }\varepsilon\le(\pi_n)_j,(\pi'_n)_j\le1-\varepsilon,\ \mathcal S_{n,i}\subseteq2^{\Gamma_{n,i}}\text{ is finite and downward closed},\ (X_{n,i},H_{n,i},E_n,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{E_n})\text{ is exactly the row geometry of }\mathrm{def:indexed-hilbert-geometry},\ (\theta_n,N_{n,z},N_{n,z}^{\ast})\text{ is exactly }\mathrm{def:indexed-target-selector-geometry},\ K_n=\prod_{i\in V_n}K_{n,i}\subset E_n\text{ is exactly }\mathrm{def:indexed-bounded-fourier-class},\text{ and }F_n,R_n^{\star}\text{ are exactly the row-specific values in }\mathrm{def:indexed-frontiers}\}\).

definitions.name: Common numerical comparison on an array
definitions.construction: For \(c_0\in(0,1]\) and \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\), define \(\mathsf C(c_0,\mathfrak A)\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[c_0F_n\le R_n^{\star}\le F_n\text{ for every }n\ge1\bigr]\). Thus one occurrence of \(c_0\) is shared by every row of the array.

definitions.name: Indexed bounded-schedule moment body
definitions.construction: For every fixed \(n\), \(\mathfrak M_n(K_n)=\operatorname{conv}\{v_n\otimes v_n:v_n\in K_n\}\subseteq\mathbb S_+^{E_n}\), where \(v_n\otimes v_n\) denotes the rank-one self-adjoint operator \(f\mapsto\langle v_n,f\rangle_{E_n}v_n\). In fixed-instance notation this is \(\mathfrak M(K)=\operatorname{conv}\{v\otimes v:v\in K\}\subseteq\mathbb S_+^E\).

definitions.name: Exact covariance-moment dual
definitions.construction: For each fixed \(n\), assignment \(z\in\Omega_n\), and \(M\in\mathbb S_+^{E_n}\), define \(\psi_{n,z}(M)=\langle\ell_n,M\ell_n\rangle_{E_n}-\langle N_{n,z}M\ell_n,(N_{n,z}MN_{n,z}^{\ast})^{\dagger}N_{n,z}M\ell_n\rangle_{V_n}\). Here \(N_{n,z}MN_{n,z}^{\ast}\) is a positive semidefinite operator on Euclidean \(\mathbb R^{V_n}\), \(\dagger\) is its Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse relative to \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V_n}\), and the convention is \(0^{\dagger}=0\); moreover \(N_{n,z}M\ell_n\in\operatorname{range}(N_{n,z}MN_{n,z}^{\ast})\), so the quadratic term is unambiguous. Define \(\mathcal D_n=\max_{M\in\mathfrak M_n(K_n)}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi_n}(z)\psi_{n,z}(M)\). Under the fixed-instance abbreviations \(E=E_n\), \(K=K_n\), \(N_z=N_{n,z}\), and \(\ell=\ell_n\), these same formulas define \(\psi_z(M)\) and \(\mathcal D\).

definitions.name: Clipped minimax incidence estimator
definitions.construction: Choose any minimizer \(a^{\star}\) of \(F\) and define \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{inc}}(z,N_zv)=\operatorname{clip}((a_z^{\star})^{\mathsf T}N_zv)\).

definitions.name: Genuine-prior posterior-ambiguity certificate
definitions.construction:
For \(\mathbf V\sim
u\), define \(\mathcal B(
u)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\,\mathbb E_{
u}[\operatorname{Var}_{
u}(	heta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V)]\) and \(\operatorname{LB}(
u)=\mathcal B(
u)\).

definitions.name: Feasible-rule upper certificate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{UB}(a)=\sup_{v\in K}\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2\).

definitions.name: Fiber-ambiguity prior-rounding handle
definitions.construction: Start from an extremal decomposition of an optimizer in \(\mathfrak M(K)\); color and symmetrize the atoms by the common fibers of the selector family \((N_z)_{z\in\Omega_n}\), then round the signed moment representation to a nonnegative probability law on \(K\) while preserving a constant fraction of average posterior ambiguity.

definitions.name: Exposure-incidence graph
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I\) is bipartite with assignment vertices \(j\in V_n\), outcome-factor vertices \(i\in V_n\), and edge \(j\sim i\) if \(j\in\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal S_i}U\).

definitions.name: Bag-local optimizer-localization handle
definitions.construction: Lift rank-one schedule moments to bag-local moments on a tree decomposition of \(\mathcal I\), carry the target-sum epigraph as a separator statistic, and eliminate assignment variables only after proving that optimal weights and moment consistency admit bag-local representatives.

definitions.name: Additive-hub separating family
definitions.construction: For \(n\ge2\), set \(\pi_j=p\), \(\pi'_j=q\), \(\Gamma_1=V_n\), \(\mathcal S_1=\{\varnothing\}\cup\{\{j\}:j\in V_n\}\), and for \(i\ge2\) set \(\Gamma_i=\{i\}\) and \(\mathcal S_i=\{\varnothing,\{i\}\}\).

definitions.name: Disjoint repeated-motif experiment
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak m^{\sqcup m}\) is formed from \(m\) disjoint copies of \(\mathfrak m\), with independent source assignments across copies, product schedule class across copies, and target equal to the arithmetic mean of the \(m\) motif targets.

definitions.name: Loomba--Eckles EAO weight and least bounded-class envelope
definitions.construction:
For every fixed instance, define the Fourier policy-shift coefficient by
\[
 \Delta_U^{\pi,\pi'}
 =\prod_{j\in U}\frac{\pi'_j-\pi_j}{\sqrt{\pi_j(1-\pi_j)}},
 \qquad \Delta_{\varnothing}^{\pi,\pi'}=1,
\]
and define the Loomba--Eckles EAO transport weight for unit \(i\) by
\[
 W_i^{\mathrm{LE}}(z)
 =\sum_{U\in\mathcal S_i}
   \Delta_U^{\pi,\pi'}\chi_{i,U}^{\pi}(z_{\Gamma_i}).
\]
The smallest uniform bounded-class second-moment envelope and the overlap degree are
\[
 B_n^{\mathrm{LE}}
 =\max_{i\in V_n}\ \sup_{v_i\in K_i}
   \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)
   \bigl(v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})W_i^{\mathrm{LE}}(z)\bigr)^2
\]
and
\[
 D_n^{\mathrm{LE}}
 =\max_{i\in V_n}
   \left|\left\{j\in V_n\setminus\{i\}:
   \Gamma_i\cap\Gamma_j\ne\varnothing\right\}\right|.
\]
Thus \(B_n^{\mathrm{LE}}\) is the least number \(B\) for which every bounded schedule in \(K\) satisfies the unitwise second-moment premise of the Loomba--Eckles spectral-overlap theorem.

definitions.name: Adaptive dual-rank and selector-fiber complexity
definitions.construction:
For a fixed admissible instance with \(F>0\), choose
\[
 M^{\star}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{M\in\mathfrak M(K)}
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\psi_z(M)
\]
having minimum rank among all maximizers, and set \(r_{\star}=\operatorname{rank}(M^{\star})\). If \(F=0\), set \(r_{\star}=1\) and do not use \(M^{\star}\). For every \(z\in\Omega_n\), define
\[
 \rho_z=\sup\{\lvert\theta(h)\rvert:h\in K,\ N_zh=0\},\qquad
 S_{\mathrm{fib}}=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\rho_z^2,
 \qquad
 m_{\mathrm{fib}}=\max_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\rho_z^2.
\]
If \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), define
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}=\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{m_{\mathrm{fib}}},
 \qquad
 \kappa=\min\{r_{\star},\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\};
\]
if \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), define \(\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}=\kappa=1\).

For every row of \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\), make the same definitions with \((F,\mathcal D,M^{\star},r_{\star},\rho_z,S_{\mathrm{fib}},m_{\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}},\kappa)\) replaced by \((F_n,\mathcal D_n,M_n^{\star},r_n,\rho_{n,z},S_{n,\mathrm{fib}},m_{n,\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_n)\) and with every fixed-instance object replaced by its row-\(n\) indexed version.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(n\) and every admissible row-\(n\) instance, the observed experiment is exactly the randomized selector experiment \(z\mapsto N_{n,z}v_n\). A minimizing indexed weight rule exists after quotienting, separately for each \(z\), the coefficient directions in \(\ker(N_{n,z}^{\ast})\), and the exact identity is \(F_n=\mathcal D_n\). Equivalently, under the fixed-instance abbreviations, \(F=\mathcal D\).
statements.justification: This reduction fixes the finite decision problem and supplies the exact dual object from which both algorithms and lower bounds must start.
statements.gap: ChenValiantValiant2020 gives a positive-semidefinite relaxation for full cubes, while LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy does not optimize jointly over assignment-indexed biased weights or bounded Fourier evaluation polytopes.
statements.consumer: The dual is the input to the genuine-prior converse and to certified risk computation for the Crépon et al. saturation design.

statements.statement: For every feasible weight rule \(a\) and every genuine prior \(\nu\in\mathcal P(K)\), \(\operatorname{LB}(\nu)\le R^{\star}\le F\le\operatorname{UB}(a)\). The clipped incidence estimator satisfies \(\sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_{\pi}(z)(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{inc}}-\theta(v))^2\le F\).
statements.justification: The certificate pair separates what is computationally verifiable from the universal comparison and prevents a signed moment functional from being mislabeled as a Bayes prior.
statements.gap: BrownCohen2021 gives a sufficient combinatorial all-estimator lower bound, but not an instance-specific posterior-variance certificate paired with the Fourier-section semilinear program.
statements.consumer: Analysts can report finite-sample certified lower and upper risk bounds even when the universal constant or exact treewidth computation is unresolved.

statements.statement: Determine whether there exists one numerical constant \(c_0>0\), independent of the population size, graph, source and target policies, Fourier supports, selector system, and triangular array, such that every admissible fixed instance satisfies \(c_0F\le R^{\star}\). Equivalently, determine whether one \(c_0\) makes \(\mathsf C(c_0,\mathfrak A)\) true for every \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\). One sufficient, but not logically necessary, route through \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{prior}}\) is to construct for every instance a symmetric genuine law \(\nu\in\mathcal P(K)\) satisfying \(\mathcal B(\nu)\ge c_0\mathcal D\). A negative resolution instead requires an explicit admissible growing family for which \(R^{\star}/F\to0\).
statements.justification: This is the remaining launch-or-kill question: whether local Fourier selector geometry permits an unbounded nonlinear advantage after the proved rank and fiber losses are exposed.
statements.gap: ChenValiantValiant2020 leaves the universal semilinear-versus-unrestricted gap open; DonohoLiuMacGibbon1990 gives a Gaussian comparison that does not transfer to noiseless selectors.
statements.consumer: A positive answer makes the linear frontier dimension-free sharp for all measurable estimators; a negative answer requires a certified growing admissible family with vanishing risk ratio.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{tw}}\), determine whether \(\operatorname{tw}(\mathcal I)\le w\) admits an exact algorithm, after augmenting incidence separators by a precisely encoded compressed global target-sum/separator state, that returns \(F\), liftable optimal weights \(a^{\star}\), and a matching moment certificate in time \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{in}})2^{O(w)}\); or whether a path or star family establishes an exact-value gap or complexity obstruction for every such compressed representation. Failure of ordinary raw edge-bag moments alone does not resolve this question.
statements.justification: The exact finite epigraph and the width-one raw-bag obstruction isolate the remaining algorithmic issue: whether the global target coupling admits a polynomial-size compressed separator state.
statements.gap: Ordinary incidence-bag moment consistency fails at treewidth one, but this proves neither optimizer nonlocality nor an exact-value or complexity lower bound; a compressed running target-sum state may still support exact elimination.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives exact risk certificates for bounded-width market and school networks; a negative answer requires a genuine exact-value or complexity obstruction and prevents raw-bag failure from being misreported as algorithmic impossibility.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p,q\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). On \(\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{hub}}\), \(F_n=\Theta(n^{-1})\) and \(R_n^{\star}=\Theta(n^{-1})\), while the Loomba--Eckles envelope is exactly
\[
 \frac{B_n^{\mathrm{LE}}(D_n^{\mathrm{LE}}+1)}{n}
 =1+n\frac{(q-p)^2}{p(1-p)}.
\]
Consequently, this envelope divided by either \(F_n\) or \(R_n^{\star}\) is \(\Theta(n)\) when \(p=q\) and \(\Theta(n^2)\) for fixed \(p\ne q\). Thus the exact frontier is strictly rate-sharper on a genuinely overlapping growing family, both on-policy and under a fixed nonzero policy shift.
statements.justification: The hub family proves that probability-weighted signed incidence geometry yields an order-\(n^{-1}\) minimax certificate even when the published maximum-overlap envelope is larger by order \(n\) on-policy and order \(n^2\) under a fixed nonzero policy shift.
statements.gap: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy, Theorem 5.1, assumes any \(B^{(n)}\) dominating all unit-summand second moments and multiplies it by \(D^{(n)}+1\); on the additive hub the least such bounded-class envelope is exactly \(1+n(q-p)^2/[p(1-p)]\) and \(D^{(n)}=n-1\).
statements.consumer: Dense-star and influencer-network analyses obtain a finite design-based certificate decaying as \(n^{-1}\), together with an exact diagnosis of how conservative the published maximum-overlap sufficient envelope is on-policy and off-policy.

statements.statement: Suppose the fixed motif \(\mathfrak m\) admits a bounded assignment-indexed linear rule \(u_{\mathfrak m}\) that is design-unbiased for the motif target at every admissible motif schedule and has one-motif worst-case mean-squared error at most \(\sigma_{\mathfrak m}^2\), and the symmetric genuine prior \(\nu_{\mathfrak m}\) has posterior ambiguity \(b_{\mathfrak m}>0\). Then for every \(m\ge1\), \(b_{\mathfrak m}/m\le R_m^{\star,\sqcup}\le F_m^{\sqcup}\le\sigma_{\mathfrak m}^2/m\).
statements.justification: This reduction recovers the familiar effective-number-of-independent-motifs rate without confusing it with a general overlap theorem.
statements.gap: CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023 uses Gaussian coefficient priors for a regular-graph lower bound, while this result tensorizes genuine bounded-schedule ambiguity for arbitrary fixed Fourier motifs.
statements.consumer: Clustered village and school experiments obtain interpretable \(1/m\) benchmarks and a calibration check for numerical certificates.

statements.statement: When \(n=1\), \(\Gamma_1=\{1\}\), and \(\mathcal S_1=2^{\{1\}}\), the full-class exact risks coincide and equal \(R^{\star}=F=(1-\pi_1)(\pi'_1)^2+\pi_1(1-\pi'_1)^2\). Pointwise, for every unknown schedule \(v\in K\) restricted by \(v_1(0)=v_1(1)\), the measurable rule \(\delta(z,N_zv)=(N_zv)_1\) has zero squared error under both assignments because \(\delta(z,N_zv)=\theta(v)\).
statements.justification: The exact base case distinguishes minimax shrinkage weights from unbiased likelihood-ratio transport, while the pointwise constant-schedule calculation checks zero error without changing the full-class minimax domain.
statements.gap: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy characterizes the minimum-norm unbiased transport weight, not the biased minimax rule even for one binary exposure.
statements.consumer: The formula is a unit test for the exact small-instance solver and for the saturation-policy implementation.

sampling_model.design: One known heterogeneous product-Bernoulli source assignment is drawn; assignment is the only randomness and all potential-outcome schedules are fixed.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population with a known graph, known local neighborhoods, and known downward-closed local Fourier supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary coordinates are mutually independent under the source law, with probabilities in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\); the target product policy is also known and interior.
sampling_model.overlap: Overlap is represented exactly by shared assignment coordinates in the local selector operators, rather than only by maximum dependency degree.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The policies, graph, neighborhoods, and support sets are known; only one schedule evaluation per unit is observed.

estimand_functional: The causal target remains \(\theta(v)\). Its exact linear-risk map is the finite convex program \[ F=\min_{\substack{t\in\mathbb R,\ a\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\left[\sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_iv_i(z_{\Gamma_i})-\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x)\right]^2\le t \] for every \(v\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\). This program has \(n2^n+1\) real variables, \(\prod_i|\operatorname{vert}(K_i)|\) listed convex quadratic constraints, an attaining weight rule \(a^{\star}\), and a matching \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\) with \(F=\mathcal D=\sum_zp_{\pi}(z)\psi_z(M)\). The all-Borel certificate is \(\max\{F/r_{\star},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\}\le R^{\star}\le F=\mathcal D\le S_{\mathrm{fib}}\), hence \(F/\kappa\le R^{\star}\le F\), where \(\rho_z=\sup\{|\theta(h)|:h\in K,\ N_zh=0\}\), \(S_{\mathrm{fib}}=\sum_zp_{\pi}(z)\rho_z^2\), \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=\max_zp_{\pi}(z)\rho_z^2\), and \(\kappa=\min\{r_{\star},S_{\mathrm{fib}}/m_{\mathrm{fib}}\}\) when \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), with the stated zero-fiber convention.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper gives a \(\pi/2\)-approximation to optimal semilinear risk and leaves open whether semilinear risk is within a universal constant of unrestricted risk.

Theorem 5.1 assumes any \(B^{(n)}\) with \(\max_i\mathbb E[(\widehat\theta_i^{(n)})^2]\le B^{(n)}\), defines \(D^{(n)}=\max_i|\{j\ne i:\Gamma_i^{(n)}\cap\Gamma_j^{(n)}\ne\varnothing\}|\), and bounds the variance by \(B^{(n)}(D^{(n)}+1)/n\).
The consistency corollary is necessary and sufficient for the Riesz estimator through the norm of its variance-characterizing operator.

For Gaussian estimation over orthosymmetric quadratically convex sets, linear minimax risk is within a factor \(1.25\) of unrestricted minimax risk; this does not transfer to noiseless randomized selectors.
Hierarchy exactness is controlled by the canonical hypergraph of the actual polynomial system, not automatically by a raw exposure-incidence graph.
The paper characterizes unrestricted network-experiment minimax risk through an estimand-specific conflict graph and gives connectivity-based bounds.

tldr: One product-Bernoulli network experiment reveals one local evaluation of each fixed bounded schedule, while the target is an average under another product policy. The proposal defines the exact assignment-indexed linear minimax risk \(F\) on the bounded local-Fourier evaluation polytopes and asks whether a structure-preserving genuine-prior argument proves \(R^{\star}\asymp F\) for every measurable estimator. A positive resolution yields an iff consistency frontier, a clipped incidence-minimax estimator, finite primal and prior certificates, a strict separation from the published degree envelope on additive hubs, and repeated-motif recovery. Incidence-treewidth exactness is retained as a separate open computational question because sparse factorization does not by itself localize the global minimax optimizer.

project_justification.gap: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy identifies the unique minimum-norm unbiased Fourier transport weight and a degree-based sufficient consistency bound, but it does not benchmark against biased linear rules or all measurable estimators. ChenValiantValiant2020 formulates the generic semilinear problem, exhibits a strict nonlinear improvement, and explicitly leaves the size of that gap open.
project_justification.niche: Product-Bernoulli local-cell selectors and downward-closed Fourier-section polytopes form a structured decision class that is neither the full-cube randomly collected-data problem nor the two-exposure conflict-graph model. Its shared fibers may permit genuine prior rounding that fails for arbitrary sampling laws.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact selector and moment dual, constructs the clipped incidence rule and certified lower and upper bounds, and concentrates the novel work in a dimension-free posterior-ambiguity rounding theorem. It then converts that comparison into an iff consistency boundary and demonstrates strict value over degree counting on an explicit overlapping family.

related_work: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy, Proposition on spectral transport and its consistency theorem, supplies the policy-indexed Fourier basis, the unbiased transport comparator, and the \(B_n(D_n+1)/n\) envelope sharpened here. ChenValiantValiant2020, Theorem 1 and Appendix D, is the closest generic formulation: it approximates semilinear risk, shows a four-coordinate strict gap, and asks whether the unrestricted gap is universally bounded. BrownCohen2021, Section 3, gives an all-estimator constant lower bound only under an alpha-non-expansion condition and therefore does not settle vanishing-risk instances. DonohoLiuMacGibbon1990 supplies the hardest-rectangle and genuine-prior comparison template in a Gaussian quadratically convex experiment, not a noiseless randomized-selector experiment. KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax characterizes unrestricted design-based risk through conflict graphs for contrastive exposures and design choice; it does not encode heterogeneous source-target transport or Fourier-section outcome classes. HarshawSavjeWang2022 characterizes consistency of the Riesz estimator through an operator norm, which motivates an exact geometric frontier but does not compare with unrestricted procedures. CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023 supplies low-order Bernoulli score and fuzzy-prior techniques for a different total-effect target. WainwrightJordan2004 and PeyrardEtAl2019 motivate the treewidth handle, but their exactness results apply only after objective and constraint locality is proved. ChinEcklesUgander2022 and CreponEtAl2013 are the empirical consumers: the proposed certificate can quantify design mismatch for stochastic seeding and saturation-policy curves.
technical_internal_limitation: The four-coordinate example in ChenValiantValiant2020 proves that semilinear and unrestricted risks need not be equal, so the comparison constant cannot be obtained from central symmetry alone. A decomposition of an optimal moment operator into rank-one atoms yields a signed or genuine mixing law, but noiseless observations may reveal the atom label and make nonlinear posterior prediction much easier than linear regression. The proposal therefore treats posterior-ambiguity-preserving rounding as the central open object. Likewise, raw incidence treewidth controls the input factorization but may fail to control the global squared target error or the assignment dependence of optimal weights; the smallest path and star systems are explicit kill tests.
honest_scope: The exact selector reduction, clipping inequality, moment-body dual, one-binary-cell formula, and generic primal/prior certificate are expected finite-dimensional results. The universal constant comparison, its iff consistency consequence, and optimizer localization at bounded raw incidence treewidth are open. The treewidth question is not used to justify the statistical frontier. At any schedule whose local outcomes are constant across assignment cells, the observed outcome vector determines the target with pointwise zero error; this fact does not set the minimax risk over the unrestricted bounded class to zero. Under one complete binary exposure the displayed full-class exact formula is recovered. General correlated assignment designs, adaptive support selection, studentization, and design optimization over an entire target-policy curve are outside the selected kernel.
